newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei shrugs off weak yen to end strong.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei shrugs off weak yen to end strong.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures mirrored gains in the Tokyo stock market and rallied towards market close to end over the key 18,000 resistance on Wednesday.
The release of Japan's December Industrial Production figures gave the benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract a boost towards 18,000 level after the market resumed trading in the afternoon.

"Its first reaction after the figures were released was to test 18,000. But it only succeeded in the second attempt. After which stop losses were triggered and brought the market up," said a dealer with a major Japanese bank.
Major stops were triggered at 18,100, 18,250, 18,300 and 18,400, the dealer said.
After hitting a high at 18,400, the March contract ended at 18,340, up 520 points from its previous close.
Turnover was moderate at 16,755 lots. Major buyers included a Wall Street trader and a Japanese institution. Both bought a total of over 700 contracts.
On Wednesday, Japan's trade ministry announced industrial production output in December rose a preliminary 0.3 percent from November.
Earlier concerns of funds unloading falling Japanese stocks also dissipated, dealers said.
Renewed buying, notably of export-oriented stocks, was triggered after the dollar climbed to over 122 yen for the first time since February 1993, they said.
The next resistance for March was now pegged at 19,300.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended flat at 307.5 on a turnover of 112 lots.
